### Lunar Base Atmospheric Thresholds & Gravity Context

The target atmospheric conditions for lunar base operations are defined as an oxygen concentration of $30\%$ ($0.30$) or higher and a total pressure of $10.2\text{ psi}$ or lower [F-005]. This baseline yields an oxygen partial pressure ($P_{\text{O2}}$) of $3.06\text{ psi}$ [C-001], representing a $43.5\%$ increase in oxygen fraction compared to standard air [C-004]. For context, Earth sea-level $P_{\text{O2}}$ is $3.07\text{ psi}$ [C-002], EVA spacesuits operate at $100\%\text{ O}_2$ at $4.3\text{ psi}$ ($P_{\text{O2}} = 4.3\text{ psi}$) [F-001], [C-003], and free-fall microgravity environments lack natural thermal buoyancy [F-008].

*Partial-Gravity Data Gap:* The NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) repository currently contains no partial-gravity combustion test data; future missions/investigations such as LUCI and FM2 are designed to address this empirical gap [F-019]. Flight experiment results from reduced-gravity platforms are published via NASA PSI [F-023].

---

### Closest Individual Experiments in NASA PSI

A scan of 536 test rows in the repository (273 fully specified tests and 263 tests with unknown $O_2$ or pressure) identified **zero tests** that simultaneously satisfied both lunar-base criteria ($O_2 \ge 0.30$ and pressure $\le 10.2\text{ psi}$). 

The individual test runs closest to these joint conditions were conducted under the **FLEX** investigation (PSI-69):

1. **Test 37** ([PSI-69:test37], [S-032 p.row 38]):
   - **Fuel:** Methanol
   - **$O_2$ Fraction:** $0.34$ ($34\%$) (meets $O_2 \ge 0.30$)
   - **Ambient Pressure:** $10.332\text{ psi}$ (exceeds the $10.2\text{ psi}$ limit by $0.132\text{ psi}$)

2. **Test 41** ([PSI-69:test41]):
   - **Fuel:** Methanol
   - **$O_2$ Fraction:** $0.30$ ($30\%$) (meets $O_2 \ge 0.30$)
   - **Ambient Pressure:** $10.332\text{ psi}$ (exceeds the $10.2\text{ psi}$ limit by $0.132\text{ psi}$)

3. **Test 38** ([PSI-69:test38]):
   - **Fuel:** Methanol
   - **$O_2$ Fraction:** $0.34$ ($34\%$) (meets $O_2 \ge 0.30$)
   - **Ambient Pressure:** $10.334\text{ psi}$ (exceeds the $10.2\text{ psi}$ limit by $0.134\text{ psi}$)

4. **Test 121** ([PSI-69:test121], [S-032 p.row 122]):
   - **Fuel:** Methanol
   - **$O_2$ Fraction:** $0.18$ ($18\%$) (shortfall of $0.12$ below $0.30$)
   - **Ambient Pressure:** $10.177\text{ psi}$ (meets the pressure limit $\le 10.2\text{ psi}$)

---

### Investigation-Level Summary (Unverified LLM Draft Notice)

*Notice:* The overall parameter boundaries listed below for investigations are compiled from an **unverified LLM draft** Golden Table.

* **FLEX**: Recorded tests bound $O_2$ fractions up to $0.34$ [S-032 p.row 20] and pressures ranging from $10.177\text{ psi}$ [S-032 p.row 122] to $44.859\text{ psi}$ [S-032 p.row 13]. FLEX focused on low-pressure ($\le 1\text{ atm}$), nitrogen-diluted ambient conditions with elevated oxygen mole fractions [S-013 p.15] to evaluate limiting oxygen index (LOI) values for spacecraft fire safety [S-013 p.8].
* **Saffire Series (Saffire-I, II, III)**: Objectives prioritized exploration atmospheres with oxygen mole fractions up to $0.34$ and reduced pressures down to $8.2\text{ psia}$ [S-020 p.7]. Saffire-I recorded test pressures between $14.4719\text{ psi}$ [S-035 p.CygnusPressureData!row 2] and $14.5369\text{ psi}$ [S-035 p.CygnusPressureData!row 293].
* **ACME-CFI-G & ACME-BRE**: Draft entries list facility capabilities covering $O_2$ ranges of $0.12$–$0.85$ (ACME-CFI-G) and $0.21$–$0.40$ (ACME-BRE), with total pressures of $6.672$–$43.511\text{ psi}$ (ACME-CFI-G) and $8.122$–$14.504\text{ psi}$ (ACME-BRE); joint per-test verification for lunar baseline compliance is not available.

---

### Repository Data Gaps

* **Unscreened Tests:** 263 of 536 PSI test rows have an unknown $O_2$ concentration or total pressure and could not be evaluated.
* **Unknown Pressure:** Total pressure is marked as unknown for **Saffire-II** and **Saffire-III**.
* **Unknown Parameters:** Both $O_2$ fraction and pressure remain unknown in the repository for **SAME**, **SAME-R**, **DAFT**, **FLEX-2**, **CFI**, and **ACME-E-FIELD**.
* **Missing Document:** **DAFT-2** has no source documentation in the repository.

facts.claim: The intermediate atmosphere for lunar operations is anticipated to feature an oxygen concentration of 30% or higher, with a total pressure of 10.2 psi or lower.
Spacesuits are pressurized with 100% oxygen up to only 4.3 psi.

In free fall, buoyancy-driven natural convection and buoyant rise of hot exhaust gases are absent, causing flames to behave dramatically differently from terrestrial flames; for example, a candle flame becomes a dim blue, spherical diffusion flame.

Currently, NASA PSI does not contain partial-gravity combustion test data. Future investigations such as the Lunar-g Combustion Investigation (LUCI) and Flammability of Materials on the Moon (FM2) are slated to address this gap.
Results from reduced-gravity combustion experiments (e.g., aboard the ISS) are made publicly available through the NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) repository.

fields.lunar_note: Range endpoints come from the flame-category ranges in Table 1; O2 ≥ 0.30 and P ≤ 10.2 psi in the same test could not be shown (no per-test table). 0.85 is the O2 in the oxidizer flowing from the burner in inverse flames, not the ambient.
Table 2.1 gives the O2 and pressure ranges separately; it could not be shown that O2 ≥ 0.30 and P ≤ 10.2 psi (≤ 0.70 bar) were met together in the same test.

Not met together in a single test (PSI-69 CSV checked row by row): among tests with O2 ≥ 0.30 the lowest pressure is 534.3 mmHg = 10.332 psi (220R001, O2 0.34, CSV row 38); the only valid test with pressure ≤ 10.2 psi, C12M101 (526.3 mmHg = 10.177 psi), has O2 0.18.

[Saffire-I, Saffire-II, Saffire-III | S-020: Operation and Development Status of the Spacecraft Fire Experiments (Saffire) | E. Flight Status and Operations Summary]
One interesting aspect of the objectives shown in Table 2 is that the fire behavior and modeling objective is a
primary objective – emphasizing the need to obtain data that can be used to extrapolate results to the different
vehicles and habitats required to perform NASA’s exploration missions. Another observation is the priority placed
on material flammability in exploration atmospheres – e.g. in ambient conditions having oxygen mole fractions up
to 0.34 and pressures of 8.2 psia. These conditions bound those considered for exploration missions. While elevated
oxygen and reduced pressure conditions are generally considered for planetary or asteroid operations where frequent
extravehicular activities (EVA) are required, the Cygnus environment provides the unique opportunity to explore
these conditions at relevant scales and obtain data that can anchor computational models that will be applied during
analysis of fire scenarios. International Conference on Environmental Systems

[General | S-026: NASA ISS Research Mini-Book: Combustion in Reduced Gravity | Ancillary Hardware Developments]
An alternative option with considerably less flexibility and scope has been proposed. It is termed the SCWO-D (for DEvice for the study of Critical LIquids and
Crystallization [DECLIC]) and envisions build-up of an insert to be installed in the
DECLIC facility. This option, because of the constraints imposed by fitting into an
existing facility, will be limited in capability and will only be able to accomplish a
subset of the science scope described above. The primary limiting features are: (i)
the reactor volume (approximately 0.5 percent of Option 1), which limits the range
of hydrodynamic studies (e.g., no bulk fluid motion); (ii) the diagnostic limitations
that are due to the reliance on existing DECLIC hardware (e.g., no Raman
spectroscopic diagnostic will eliminate chemical kinetic studies); (iii) a single optical
axis, making simultaneous reaction zone and precipitate transport observations
difficult if not impossible; and (iv) experiments may be limited to “quasi-steady”
processes since constant pressure conditions will be difficult to maintain for any
significant time because of the volume limitations. New Initiatives
Besides the SoFIE and ACME experiments planned to be conducted in CIR on the
ISS, there are a number of new combustion initiatives that are envisioned for future
ISS research. Some of these may be undertaken more readily in the near term as spinoffs of existing research since they require relatively smaller resources and hence may
be faster to develop.

[FLEX | S-013: NASA/TP-2015-216046 Detailed Results from FLEX | Unknown section]
Most of the tests were
conducted at pressures between 0.7 and 1 atm, and many of the
tests were in air. A principle objective was to determine the
limiting oxygen index (LOI), the oxygen percentage below which
combustion would not occur. This objective reflected the FLEX
focus on investigating fire safety in spacecraft. Observed LOI
values for these fuels appear to be slightly lower than initially
expected. Besides documenting both radiative extinction at
higher dilutions and diffusive extinctions at lower dilutions for
both fuels, the results exhibited disruptive extinctions and
provided information pertinent to soot production for heptane. The continuing experiments are providing additional data for
these two fuels, as well as droplet-combustion data for other
fuels, and NASA intends to catalog these data in similar reports.

rules.rule: Do NOT extrapolate microgravity results directly to Lunar or Martian gravity without explicitly stating the lack of direct partial-gravity empirical data and explaining bounding logic ([F-019], [F-021]).

When queried regarding combustion in Lunar or Martian gravity, explicitly clarify that NASA PSI currently contains no partial-gravity test data [F-019]. Mention E-FIELD electric field chemi-ion simulation [F-020] and 0-g/1-g bounding methodology [F-021] if relevant.

Never assess spacecraft fire flammability solely on oxygen percentage. Always evaluate oxygen partial pressure (via calculation), total pressure, diluent inert species (N2, CO2, He), and ventilation forced flow velocity together.
If asked about rocket engine or thruster propellant fires, clearly state that propulsion systems are outside the scope of PSI microgravity science due to momentum-dominated flow regimes [F-022].

For every experimental finding reported, cite the exact test conditions: fuel type, geometry, oxygen concentration, ambient pressure, flow velocity, and hardware facility. If a condition is omitted in the source, label it as 'unspecified'; do NOT guess.
If an empirical value or data point is absent from the indexed chunks and Golden Table, state 'data not available in repository'. Never fabricate numerical values from LLM parametric memory.
When source documents report conflicting findings or values, present both sources with their respective document citations, PI names, and publication years; do not arbitrarily select one.

Clearly distinguish between empirical flight experiment findings (PSI / peer-reviewed reports), challenge guidelines, mathematical derivations, and speculative engineering hypotheses. Never present interpretation as an empirical fact.
